source: NCERT Class XI, An Introduction to Indian Art (Part 1), Ch. 6 (Temple Architecture and Sculpture).

sections.heading: 1. Temple — Basic Parts
points: Core parts of a Hindu temple: **garbhagriha** (sanctum, houses the deity), **mandapa** (hall for devotees), **shikhara/vimana** (tower over the sanctum), **antarala** (vestibule), **amalaka/kalasha** (crowning elements), **gopuram** (gateway tower, south).
Temples became elaborate from the **Gupta period** onward; two broad styles: **Nagara (north)** and **Dravida (south)**, with **Vesara** as a hybrid.

sections.heading: 2. Nagara (North Indian) Style
points: **Nagara** — curvilinear **shikhara**, built on a raised platform, usually without large enclosure walls/gateways.

Sub-schools/examples: **Odisha (Kalinga)** — Lingaraja (Bhubaneswar), **Konark Sun Temple**, Jagannath (Puri); **Khajuraho (Chandela)** — Kandariya Mahadeva; **Central India, Rajasthan (Dilwara Jain temples), Gujarat (Modhera Sun temple)**.
Khajuraho temples known for erotic and elaborate sculpture.

sections.heading: 3. Dravida (South Indian) Style
points: **Dravida** — pyramidal tower called **vimana**; enclosed within a **compound wall** with towering **gopurams (gateways)**; a **water tank**.
**Pallavas** — Mahabalipuram (Shore temple, rathas); **Cholas** — the **Brihadeshwara (Rajarajeshwara) temple at Thanjavur** (Rajaraja I) with a huge vimana.
Later, **Vijayanagara (Hampi)** and **Nayaka** temples had enormous gopurams and pillared halls.

sections.heading: 4. Vesara and Regional Styles
points: **Vesara** — a hybrid of Nagara and Dravida, seen in the **Deccan (Chalukyas, Rashtrakutas, Hoysalas)**.
**Chalukyas of Badami** — Aihole, Badami, Pattadakal (a UNESCO site).
**Hoysalas** — Belur, Halebid (star-shaped plan, soapstone, intricate carving).
**Ellora Kailasa temple (Rashtrakuta)** — monolithic rock-cut temple.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Nagara (north) = curvilinear shikhara; Dravida (south) = pyramidal vimana + gopuram; Vesara = hybrid (Deccan).
Garbhagriha = sanctum; gopuram = gateway tower (south).
Konark (Sun Temple, Odisha), Khajuraho (Chandela) = Nagara; Brihadeshwara Thanjavur (Chola) = Dravida.
Hoysala temples (Belur, Halebid) = star-shaped, soapstone.
Kailasa temple, Ellora = monolithic (Rashtrakuta).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Nagara = shikhara (curvilinear)**; **Dravida = vimana + gopuram**; **Vesara = hybrid**.
**Gopuram** = the tall **gateway tower** of South Indian temples.
**Brihadeshwara temple (Thanjavur)** was built by the **Cholas (Rajaraja I)**.
The **Kailasa temple at Ellora** is a **monolithic** (single-rock) temple by the Rashtrakutas.
